Because a leaking lower tank saturates its own loop at 12 V, this threshold catches sustained/severe leaks but misses the milder leak phases where effort settles between roughly 9.5 and 11.4 V (tank1_leak t1=91 missed, tank2_leak phase around t=280-330 t2 missed). It also has no hysteresis on the flag, so as soon as the effort dips one call below 11.5 V the flag drops off while the fault persists (both_leaks t1 missed from t=260), and it has no positive leak evidence other than extreme effort. Meanwhile the setpoint reduction gradually pulls the tank down, which lowers the demand and the effort, so the supervisor's own mitigation erases the very signal it uses to detect the leak, causing the flag to fall and the fault to be missed. Conversely, the restore path keys on 'eff1_low and sp1 < nom1', and after a mitigation the effort is genuinely low, so setpoints are stepped back toward nominal while the fault is still active, producing the flip-flop and residual restore_gap (0.04-0.18 m). No false positive on baseline because the healthy settled effort ranges (tank1 8.79-10.54 V, tank2 8.52-9.26 V) never reach 11.5 V; but the pure-threshold detector also produces false positives on the OTHER tank after one tank's leak clears, when effort momentarily exceeds 11.5 V during the recovery transient (tank2_leak t1 false_pos=50 around t=490-540, when tank1 effort rose to 11.5 V as tank2 recovered).
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the single fixed effort threshold with per-tank, level-relative leak evidence that combines (a) loop effort above a per-tank elevated band that is high relative to healthy mean and trending/sustained, and (b) the tank level sitting below its active setpoint despite the elevated effort, so a genuine leak remains detectable through setpoint mitigation. Add an asymmetry so that elevated effort in one loop is attributed to that loop's tank only when that loop's own level error is also elevated, preventing cross-loop false positives during the other tank's recovery transient. Use hysteresis counters (enter on K consecutive calls, exit only after several consecutive clear calls) for both flags and gate setpoint restoration on the flag being cleared plus effort returning near the healthy mean, so setpoints are not restored while a fault is still active.
relations_learned: A mitigated setpoint lowers pump demand, so effort-alone detectors lose the leak signal; detection must use level-versus-setpoint error.
Effort in one loop spikes above healthy mean during the other tank's fault recovery, so per-loop flags need own-loop level evidence.

self_check: Threshold checks against measured fault-free reference. tank1 settled healthy mean|error|=0.0154, range [-0.0062, 0.0736]; effort mean 9.35 V, range [8.79, 10.54] V. tank2 settled healthy mean|error|=0.0202, range [0.0019, 0.0495]; effort mean 8.96 V, range [8.52, 9.26] V. Start-up healthy mean|error| tank1=0.1262 (range 0.0743-0.1558), tank2=0.1091 (range 0.0499-0.1531); effort tank1 range [4.15, 10.59] V, tank2 [6.08, 8.76] V. My entry condition for tank1 requires BOTH mean effort over the last 5 samples > 10.6 V (above healthy settled max 10.54 V by 0.06 V, so healthy can barely reach it; start-up max 10.59 V excluded by requiring the level below setpoint AND requiring 3 consecutive calls) AND current error (setpoint - level) > 0.07 m (above healthy settled max 0.0736 m only marginally, and above mean|e| 0.0154 by 4.5x; start-up mean|e| up to 0.1558 is excluded because during start-up the level is below setpoint for a reason and effort is only briefly high, so the 3-call streak plus the 10.6 V effort gate rejects it: during start-up tank1 effort is below 10.6 V for most rows). For tank2 I require mean effort > 9.5 V (above healthy settled max 9.26 V by 0.24 V) AND error > 0.075 m (above healthy settled max 0.0495 m by 1.5x; start-up tank2 mean|e| up to 0.1531 m is rejected because tank2 effort during start-up never exceeds 8.76 V, below the 9.5 V gate). Exit requires 4 consecutive calls with effort below 10.2 V (tank1) / 9.2 V (tank2) AND error below 0.06 m, so the flag is sticky and does not chatter on one noisy sample; the 0.06 m exit threshold is above the healthy settled error maxima (0.0736 tank1, 0.0495 tank2) only for tank2, so tank1 exit also needs the effort to fall back below 10.2 V (healthy settled mean 9.35 V) which is the stronger signal. All gates are above the respective healthy settled effort maxima, giving zero false positives on the fault-free settled reference.
proposed_change: Replace the single fixed effort threshold with a per-tank sticky leak detector combining sustained elevated loop effort (tank1 > ~10.6 V, tank2 > ~9.5 V over the last 5 samples) with own-loop level error above a healthy-settled maximum (tank1 > 0.07 m, tank2 > 0.075 m), entering after 3 consecutive calls and clearing only after 4 consecutive clear calls, so effort dips caused by the supervisor's own setpoint mitigation do not drop the flag. Restore a tank's setpoint toward nominal only when its flag is clear and its effort has returned to the healthy band, and step setpoints down more slowly (0.015 m) to keep the mitigation from hiding the fault while reducing restore_gap.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The current supervisor relies on absolute effort thresholds (10.6/9.5 V) and error thresholds that are only valid at the nominal setpoint; once it lowers a setpoint to mitigate a leak, the error collapses and the flag chatters (on/off every 10 s), causing missed anomalies while the fault is still active, and after the fault clears it restores setpoints too slowly, leaving a large restore_gap. In both_leaks it also falsely flags tank1 during the fault-free recovery period because effort (10.1-10.6 V) transiently exceeds 10.6 V while the setpoint is below nominal.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Make the anomaly decision depend on the leak-induced effort-vs-level relationship (effort high while level is pinned near the clamped setpoint floor) rather than absolute error, and restore setpoints faster once the fault clears.

self_check: Start-up transient (t=1-199s): tank1 effort range [4.15,10.59] V, mean 9.15 V; tank2 effort range [6.08,8.76] V, mean 8.27 V. My enter thresholds (effort>11.2 V sustained 3 samples for tank1; >10.5 V sustained 3 for tank2) are above the observed start-up maxima, so no false positives. Settled: tank1 effort range [8.79,10.54] V, tank2 [8.52,9.26] V; enter thresholds 11.2/10.5 exceed these settled maxima, so no false positives. Healthy settled mean|error| tank1 0.0154, tank2 0.0202; my error-floor condition requires level within 0.02 m of the setpoint AND effort above the enter threshold, which does not occur in healthy data (effort stays below 10.6 V). Clear thresholds (effort<9.6 V for tank1, <8.9 V for tank2) are near but above settled means (9.35/8.96 V) and are only used while a flag is held, minimizing false clears. Sustained fault effort saturates at 12 V, well above enter thresholds, so missed anomalies are reduced.
proposed_change: Replace absolute error thresholds with a leak signature based on loop effort exceeding a high threshold (11.2 V tank1, 10.5 V tank2) for at least 3 consecutive samples, using effort/level trend rather than raw error so setpoint reductions do not break detection. Increase restore step and use clear thresholds below the settled effort means (effort<9.6 V tank1, <8.9 V tank2) plus level within 0.02 m of nominal target to decide a fault has cleared, so flags clear promptly and setpoints return to nominal faster.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor's hysteresis uses absolute effort thresholds (EFF1_LEAK=10.6, EFF2_LEAK=9.5) that only fire on saturation, so mild leaks that keep effort below those cutoffs are missed, and the persistent-low-setpoint state makes flags latch on/off (chatter) long after the fault clears, producing false positives and large restore gaps.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace fixed voltage thresholds with per-window relative criteria (rise from the window's own baseline plus sustained high decile) combined with a leak-consistent error sign, and add a true clear condition based on effort returning near window baseline and error near zero, so flags reset and setpoints restore fully.

self_check: Healthy reference: start-up (t=1-199) tank1 mean|error|=0.1262 (range .0743-.1558), tank2 0.1091 (range .0499-.1531); settled (t>=200) tank1 mean|error|=0.0154 (range -.0062..0.0736), tank2 0.0202 (range .0019-.0495). Healthy settled efforts: tank1 mean 9.35 V range [8.79,10.54]; tank2 mean 8.96 V range [8.52,9.26]; start-up efforts tank1 mean 9.15 range [4.15,10.59], tank2 mean 8.27 range [6.08,8.76]. My thresholds: leak enter requires effort_min10 > window_min + 1.2 V AND effort_min10 > 9.6 V AND effort_max3 >= 10.8 V AND error_mean10 > 0.07 (tank1) / effort_min10 > 8.8 V AND effort_max3 >= 9.8 V AND error_mean10 > 0.07 (tank2). Healthy settled max effort tank1 10.54 V never exceeds 10.8 V and tank2 9.26 V never reaches 9.8 V, and healthy |error| stays below 0.0736 so enters are avoided; that means 0 false positives on baseline. Start-up errors up to 0.1558 can exceed 0.07, but start-up efforts never stay 1.2 V above the window minimum while also spiking above 10.8/9.8 V for three consecutive windows, so start-up false enters are also avoided. Clear requires effort_min10 < window_min + 0.8 V AND effort_min10 < 9.4 V (tank1) / < 8.8 V (tank2) AND error_mean10 < 0.02, which healthy settled values satisfy, restoring setpoints to nominal with near-zero gap.
proposed_change: Use window-relative effort rise plus saturation spike and sustained positive tracking error as the tank-specific anomaly entrance, with a clear condition when effort returns near the window baseline and error drops below 0.02. This tracks both mild and severe leaks, stops flag chatter, and fully restores setpoints to nominal once each fault clears.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor uses instantaneous single-call conditions (eff1_recent > 10.6 and err1 > 0.07) that are not satisfied exactly at fault onset, so the initial transient of the leak is missed. Once the setpoint is lowered to reduce h1, the error collapses and the leak flag drops out while the fault is still active (missed events), and after fault clearance the slow setpoint restoration leaves a restore_gap. The require-both-effort-and-error logic also causes false positives in both_leaks when the other loop's effort temporarily rises; the fixed step sizes cause chatter and slow recovery.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Use a sustained-effort window test (e.g. mean effort over several samples above a conservative threshold) together with a monotonic error growth test, and restore setpoints aggressively once the effort-based clear condition is met; verify the effort thresholds against the start-up transient to avoid false positives.

self_check: Healthy effort thresholds: tank1 enter at 11.0 V, tank2 enter at 10.5 V. In the reference fault-free run, tank1 settled effort range [8.79,10.54] V, peak start-up 10.59 V, so 11.0 is above both by 0.41–0.46 V. Tank2 settled effort range [8.52,9.26] V, peak start-up 8.76 V, so 10.5 V is above both by 1.24–1.74 V. Error thresholds: combined score require |err| > 0.060 for tank1 and > 0.055 for tank2; healthy settled mean|error| is 0.0154 (tank1) and 0.0202 (tank2), start-up means are 0.1262 and 0.1091 but the start-up period is masked by a level-slope/trajectory test, so no false positive. Clear thresholds: tank1 effort < 9.8 V and |err| < 0.045; tank2 effort < 9.6 V and |err| < 0.045, which are above healthy settled ranges and below leak saturation, allowing reliable restore.
proposed_change: Replace the single-sample effort/error tests with sustained rolling-window tests: compute 10-sample mean effort and error, and flag a tank when its mean effort exceeds a conservative threshold together with a consistent error sign or a level not converging; clear when mean effort falls below a slightly lower threshold. Restore setpoints in larger steps and immediately once the fault-clear condition is met, using the effort history to hold the flag through setpoint-induced error collapse.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor's leak criteria demanded simultaneous high loop effort (>10.6V) AND high tracking error, but once the supervisor lowers the setpoint during a fault the tracking error collapses, so ongoing leaks register as cleared. This caused oscillating flags (false positives) and long stretches of missed anomalies in both_leaks and tank1_leak; the both_leaks trace shows tank2's loop effort rising to 12V at t=220-330s is the only reliable, setpoint-independent leak signature, and tank1's own effort swinging between 9.7 and 10.7V after setpoint reduction was repeatedly misread as 'clear'.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Decouple the leak-exit criterion from tracking error and depend on sustained high loop effort (near the 12V saturation) plus the level's persistent departure from the (reduced) setpoint, and only restore setpoints after several consecutive seconds with the loop effort back inside its healthy settled range.

self_check: Healthy loop effort settled ranges measured: tank1 (pump2) mean 9.35V, max 10.54V; tank2 (pump1) mean 8.96V, max 9.26V. Start-up effort ranges: tank1 4.15-10.59V, tank2 6.08-8.76V. Proposed leak threshold for tank1 loop is 10.9V (above 10.59 start-up max and 10.54 settled max), for tank2 loop 9.6V (above 8.76 start-up max and 9.26 settled max). Healthy level errors settled: tank1 -0.0062..0.0736, tank2 0.0019..0.0495; start-up mean|e| up to 0.13/0.11. A level must stay more than 0.04 m below its active setpoint for several samples to count as a leak, which start-up never holds (errors shrink continuously).
proposed_change: Replace error-gated leak entry with a sustained-loop-effort test (tank1 loop >10.9V, tank2 loop >9.6V) plus a persistent level deficit from the active setpoint, and hold the flag as long as that effort stays elevated; only clear and restore a setpoint after 5 consecutive samples with loop effort below the healthy settled ceiling. This stops the setpoint-lowering from erasing the leak signal.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The entry tests gate on level error (>0.07/0.075 m) which the supervisor's own setpoint trimming suppresses, and the fixed enter/exit streaks flip the held flag between calls, so mild leaks in tank1_leak/both_leaks are missed (68/49/34 events) and the false positives cluster where effort sits just above 10.5 V during recovery. Restore steps of 0.01 m leave 0.035-0.060 m restore gaps in the cleared scenarios.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Score each tank on its own loop's effort versus a slow baseline plus a sustained positive tracking-error/deficit term that survives setpoint trimming, and make the exit condition a proper hysteresis pair (low effort AND small deficit) rather than a single-sample streak.

self_check: Healthy settled effort: t1 range [8.79,10.54] mean 9.35 (t2 [8.52,9.26] mean 8.96); start-up effort t1 mean 9.15 range [4.15,10.59], t2 mean 8.27 range [6.08,8.76]. My entry requires t1 loop >=10.7 V and t2 loop >=9.5 V sustained for 4+ samples (t1 excursion above 10.54 reached only ~0.1 s in healthy data, so no false positive; t2 9.5 V clears healthy max 9.26 by 0.24 V). Exit requires effort <10.2/9.1 V AND deficit <0.02 m for 3 samples, both inside healthy bounds. Effort must exceed baseline+0.45 V to defeat start-up ramp false flags.
proposed_change: Detect each lower-tank leak from its own loop's sustained effort rise above a healthy-envelope threshold, confirmed by a level deficit versus the active setpoint, and keep the flag while effort stays high through setpoint trimming; use an asymmetric hysteresis exit (low effort plus small deficit) before stepping the setpoint back toward nominal in larger 0.02 m increments.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor detects leaks using absolute thresholds on 5-sample mean effort and instantaneous error, but it trims setpoints downward whenever a flag is held, which suppresses the tracking error that the entry test requires. This creates flag chatter: the flag clears, error rises again, flag re-enters, and each clear/enter cycle around the true fault interval produces both missed and false-positive seconds. Misses dominate tank1_leak (68 s) because once the setpoint is trimmed low, effort falls back to ~10 V, below the 10.6 V entry threshold, even though the tank is still leaking. False positives appear whenever setpoint is restored above nominal (0.295-0.35 in both_leaks) and the loop works hard against the residual level deficit; effort then exceeds 10.6 V with error above 0.06 while no fault exists.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Make flag entry depend on effort margin above a setpoint-compensated baseline rather than absolute error, and use hysteresis with a minimum hold time so the flag cannot drop inside a fault interval while the setpoint is trimmed.
relations_learned: Trimming a leaking tank's setpoint lowers its own loop effort, so absolute effort thresholds lose the leak signature and cause missed detections.
Restoring setpoint above nominal makes a healthy loop work hard with positive error, mimicking a leak and causing false positives.

self_check: Healthy settled (t>=200 s) reference: tank1 mean|e|=0.0154, range [-0.0062, 0.0736], effort mean 9.35 V, range [8.79,10.54] V; tank2 mean|e|=0.0202, range [0.0019,0.0495], effort mean 8.96 V, range [8.52,9.26] V. Start-up (t<200 s): tank1 mean|e|=0.1262, max 0.1558, effort up to 10.59 V; tank2 mean|e|=0.1091, max 0.1531, effort 6.08-8.76 V. My thresholds must exceed 10.54 V (tank1) and 9.26 V (tank2) to avoid settled false positives, and my error gate must exceed 0.1558/0.1531 to avoid start-up false positives; I therefore use effort thresholds 10.9 V (tank1) and 9.45 V (tank2), an error gate of 0.09 during start-up and 0.06 when settled, plus a 5-of-7 window vote and hold time. This keeps baseline_no_fault at zero false positives while catching effort saturation near 12 V during true leaks (e.g. 11.2-12.0 V in tank1_leak).
proposed_change: Replace instantaneous single-sample tests with a 7-sample window vote: require at least 5 samples above the effort threshold and 2 samples with error above a start-up-aware error gate, plus a minimum 6-call hold once set. Release only after 6 consecutive calls below a lower effort threshold and small error, and only restore setpoints when no fault is indicated on either tank.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The effort thresholds (EFF1_LEAK=10.6, EFF2_LEAK=9.5) are too close to the healthy settled means (tank1 loop 9.35 V, tank2 loop 8.96 V) and the effort condition is ANDed with an error condition that the supervisor itself destroys by trimming the setpoint; once the setpoint is lowered until the tank's level sits only ~0.03-0.05 m below the trimmed setpoint, error collapses below ERR1_LEAK/ERR2_LEAK and the flag drops even though the leak is still active (t=270-350 s of both_leaks). Combined with the 10 s flag hold and the 3-5 sample streaks, this produces 49-68 missed counts per leaking tank, and the ERR_CLEAR/EFF_CLEAR exit chords fire on healthy post-fault restoration (t=530-570 s of both_leaks) to add false positives.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Drop error from the detection condition entirely and use only the leaking tank's own loop effort: flag when the 10 s mean effort exceeds a threshold safely above the healthy mean but below saturation (T1 ~9.9 V vs healthy 9.35 V, T2 ~9.35 V vs healthy 8.96 V) for a short run, and clear when the same mean drops below a lower hysteresis band (T1 9.55 V, T2 9.05 V). Treat setpoint below nominal as evidence-of-fault for latching, not as the detector, and gate restore on a multi-call effort-and-error recovery.

self_check: Healthy windows the leak test must not fire on: start-up transient (t=1-199 s): tank1 loop effort mean 9.15 V, range [4.15, 10.59] V; tank2 loop effort mean 8.27 V, range [6.08, 8.76] V. Settled (t>=200 s): tank1 loop effort mean 9.35 V, range [8.79, 10.54] V; tank2 loop effort mean 8.96 V, range [8.52, 9.26] V. My new enter thresholds are T1_ENTER=9.90 V and T2_ENTER=9.35 V; the T1 threshold sits above the settled mean 9.35 V and inside the settled max 10.54 V (a single-sample 10.54 V could enter, so I require the 10 s mean over 10 s > 9.90 V, which the 10 s-mean healthy tail at 9.35 V cannot satisfy), and the T2 threshold 9.35 V sits above the settled mean 8.96 V and above the settled max 9.26 V, so a 10 s mean cannot reach it in the healthy case. Start-up means (9.15 V and 8.27 V) are both below the enter thresholds, so start-up does not trip them; the 10 s-mean filter also averages away the brief start-up effort spikes that a single sample would otherwise catch. Exit bands T1_CLEAR=9.55 V, T2_CLEAR=9.05 V are below the enter bands and above the healthy means, giving clean hysteresis without chattering on the noise-free signal.
proposed_change: Replace the error-gated effort test with a sustained own-loop-effort test: flag tank N when its 10 s mean loop effort exceeds T1_ENTER=9.90 V (tank1 loop / pump2, effort field 'tank1.pump_effort') or T2_ENTER=9.35 V (tank2 loop / pump1, effort field 'tank2.pump_effort'), and clear only when the same 10 s mean falls below T1_CLEAR=9.55 V / T2_CLEAR=9.05 V. Keep the setpoint-lower behavior while the flag is up, latch the flag for the whole call interval once entered, and restore each setpoint toward nominal only after the effort has stayed below the clear band for the whole window and the level is within 0.02 m of nominal.

failure_analysis.what_failed: Anomaly detection uses absolute effort/error thresholds that the supervisor's own setpoint trimming defeats: once setpoints are lowered, the leaking tank's error and effort fall back into the healthy range, so flags chatter (tank1_leak: 68 missed, flag toggling every call between t=280-400 s) and, in both_leaks, tank2's leak is missed for the whole early phase (t=210-220 s) because detection requires BOTH a 10.6 V effort and a 0.07 error, while the offset-coupling makes tank2's loop effort lag. False positives in both_leaks at t=530-570 s come from residual effort above 10.6 V during setpoint restoration, not a real fault.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace fixed absolute-effort gating with a setpoint-independent effort-excess measure: compare each loop's effort to the healthy closed-loop effort it should need at the CURRENT setpoint given the other loop's setpoint (a static feedforward/steady-state model), so a leak is the residual, not the raw voltage. This keeps detection invariant to trims and restores, and prevents restore-phase false positives.

self_check: Healthy settled effort: tank1 loop mean 9.35 V range [8.79,10.54], tank2 loop mean 8.96 V range [8.52,9.26]. My effective thresholds: tank1 flag needs effort exceeding the predicted need at the current setpoint by >0.9 V (so raw effort must stay >10.25 V at nominal sp=0.30; healthy max 10.54 V is only briefly exceeded at the start of the settled phase, hence the required 3-sample persistence and the extra requirement that the level is NOT converging, i.e. 10-sample level slope < 0.003 m/s or level deficit > 0.02 m — in healthy settled operation tank1 level reaches 0.30 and slope ~0). tank2 flag needs effort excess >0.7 V (raw >9.66 V at nominal, above healthy max 9.26 V) plus non-convergence. During start-up transient (t=1-199 s), tank1 error range [0.0743,0.1558], mean 0.1262, effort up to 10.59 V and tank2 effort up to 8.76 V — the start-up effort is below my 10.25/9.66 thresholds and the levels are converging monotonically, so no false positive; I additionally gate on abs(error) drop over the window (<0.02 improvement) so monotone start-up convergence cannot trigger. Clear condition requires effort within 0.5 V of the setpoint-predicted need AND leveled slope for 4 samples, tolerating the small step transient when a fault genuinely stops.
proposed_change: Detect a leak as a setpoint-invariant effort EXCESS relative to the steady-state effort predicted for the current setpoint pair, combined with non-convergence of the level (flat or falling slope with a persistent deficit). Clear and begin setpoint restoration only after the effort excess collapses toward the predicted need for several consecutive samples, with asymmetric hysteresis, so setpoint trimming and restoration no longer defeat detection or manufacture false positives.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor uses fixed absolute effort thresholds tuned to the settled setpoint (0.3/0.35) but then trims setpoints, which lowers the effort on the leaking loop below those thresholds. Since the setpoint stays below nominal while the leak persists, the 'enter' path is never reachable again, so the flag must be continuously maintained by the 'not clear' branch. The clear branch fires whenever the trimmed loop effort dips below EFF_CLEAR (10.2/9.2 V) together with a small error, causing chattering (both_leaks t1 false positives 30, missed 49; tank1_leak missed 68) and slow restore. The leak also drags the other loop's effort down, so the non-leaking tank is not flagged but stays mis-restored.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Replace the second path's reliance on absolute effort after setpoint trim with a leak detector anchored to the active setpoint, using the PI tracking error of the leaking loop relative to its steady-state error at nominal as the invariable signature. Because the leak suppresses effective outflow area, its own loop cannot hold the setpoint even at saturation; a persistent positive error of >~0.02 m with effort above 9.8 V at nominal-relative setpoints is the leak signature.

self_check: Healthy settled operation (no supervisor): tank1 loop effort range [8.79, 10.54] V, mean 9.35 V, mean|error|=0.0154, max error=0.0736. tank2 loop effort range [8.52, 9.26] V, mean 8.96 V, mean|error|=0.0202, max error=0.0495. Start-up transient: tank1 effort [4.15, 10.59] V, mean 9.15, mean|error|=0.1262, max|error|=0.1558; tank2 effort [6.08, 8.76] V, mean 8.27, mean|error|=0.1091, max|error|=0.1531. My enter conditions are (active-sp-based) effort_recent > 10.6 V for tank1 loop (above the healthy settled max 10.54 V and above the start-up max 10.59 V) AND mean|error| over the last 5 samples > 0.025 m (above settled mean 0.0154) AND the level has not recovered after a 10 s setpoint trim (so setpoint-relative deficit > 0.02 m). The non-leaking tank's effort dropped below 8.8 V in both_leaks (t2 5-sample mean 8.2-6.1 V), which stays inside its healthy start-up range [6.08, 8.76] so tank2's baseline tolerance is safe. Restore uses a 0.02 m step per 10 s call, and the flag is held until either the leaking loop's effort_drop (relative to the pre-trim mean) exceeds 1.2 V with the level tracking its setpoint for 40 consecutive samples. The absolute-threshold approach this replaces matched the healthy settled start-up max (10.59 V), causing false positives at t=530-570 in both_leaks.
proposed_change: Re-parameterize the leak detector to be anchored to the active setpoint: flag tank N when its own loop effort stays above 10.6 V (above the healthiest max 10.59 V observed) for 4 consecutive 1 s samples while the active setpoint is at or below nominal and the level deficit relative to that setpoint exceeds 0.02 m for at least 3 s. Clear only after the loop effort has collapsed at least 1.5 V below the trimmed-setpoint plateau and the deficit has fallen below 0.01 m for 4 consecutive calls, and use slower restore steps (0.005 m/s) when the leak has not cleared, 0.02 m/s once cleared.

failure_analysis.what_failed: The supervisor's leak detection relies on the leaking tank's own loop effort staying above an absolute threshold while its error stays above a fixed gate. As soon as the supervisor trims the leaking tank's setpoint, both effort and error fall below those thresholds, so the flag chatters (missed events like t=270-350 in both_leaks, t=290-400 in tank1_leak). Because it also trims setpoints without regard for the non-leaking tank, it drags the healthy tank's setpoint down, then during recovery raises it in small steps that keep the loop effort high enough to re-trigger false positives (t=530-570 in both_leaks). Cross-coupling makes the non-leaking tank's effort drop, so holding the leak flag must not depend on that tank's effort.
failure_analysis.next_recommendation: Detect a leak from the SUM of the two loop efforts and the leaking tank's absolute effort deficit relative to the other tank, using setpoint-independent effort thresholds, and only trim the leaking tank's setpoint; restore both setpoints as soon as the flag clears, because the sum test is insensitive to cross-coupled effort shifts.
failure_analysis.self_check: Healthy start-up (t=1-199s): tank1 effort mean 9.15 V range [4.15, 10.59]; tank2 effort mean 8.27 V range [6.08, 8.76]; sum effort approx mean 17.4 V range up to 19.35 V. Healthy settled (t>=200s): tank1 effort mean 9.35 V range [8.79, 10.54]; tank2 effort mean 8.96 V range [8.52, 9.26]; sum effort range [17.3, 19.8] V. My leak thresholds: own-loop effort > 11.5 V AND sum (tank1+tank2 effort) > 20.0 V. These are above the healthy maxima (10.54 V own, ~19.8 V sum) so cannot false-positive; a leak saturating a pump at 12 V pushes the sum above 20 V, satisfying the condition. Clear thresholds: sum < 18.5 V (below start-up max 19.35 V) and own effort < 9.6 V, so a leaking-tank flag clears only when the leak truly ends.

proposed_change: Replace the absolute single-tank effort/error tests with a setpoint-independent test that flags a tank when its own loop effort stays above 11.5 V and the combined effort of both loops exceeds 20.0 V; this survives setpoint trimming and cross-coupling.
